description.value: A long-winged flyer of the permanent storm belt that cannot get airborne in calm air and does not try, riding the shear at the belt margin for weeks at a stretch. It comes down on the flats only to lay, and then only on the two or three nights a year when the belt slackens, which is when almost all of them are taken. The local calendar names those nights after the bird rather than the other way round.
